analysis:
Examined the docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md head text and its only changed region (lines 670-690, the new demanded-latest checkpoint paragraph and the date bump). Also examined the new helper EngineV2Factory.demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens in EngineV2Factory+DemandedCheckpoint.swift (head lines 61-79), and the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer bump (aee6ebb -> 76ff231).

Security behavior of the helper: it is a scheduling-geometry change only. It returns a non-nil minimum only for the .paged backend, a dense Qwen3.5 model, and an SSDHybridCheckpointStore whose backendLayout is paged or nativeQuantizedPaged. Otherwise it returns nil. It sets no new encryption, key, tenant or scope handling. The checkpoint boundary only changes where captures end. Per the doc, authentication, HMAC lookup tags, cacheSalt scoping, store floor, write-budget and retention limits (at most 3 boundaries) remain unchanged. This is consistent with the T-041 posture: at-rest artifacts are still encrypted, HMAC-named and TTL-bound. No change to TTL, disk budget, name derivation, AAD or purge points is visible, so no SEC-035 re-sign-off trigger is visible.

Availability and side-channel considerations: the extra range cut may add one more checkpoint capture and write per eligible request. This is bounded by the existing byte-admission and write-budget limits and the documented 1/8 and 1/16 staging caps. It also gives slightly finer prefix reuse, which marginally extends the same-account TTFT oracle (SEC-035) in kind but not in scope. This is not a new finding.

Unverified: the submodule bump contents (DemandedShortCheckpointRange.swift, the CBv2SchedulerConfig field, the scheduler changes) are not supplied as a diff, so the claimed token-exact restore and the safety of the scheduling change cannot be verified here. The head file's call-site wiring of the new helper into the engine config is not visible. Integration should confirm that the SDK-side demandedLatest range logic cannot cut below the store floor or desynchronize the projection from the scheduler, and that the submodule update introduces no other security-relevant changes.
